definition: A tree of cryptographic hashes in which each leaf is the hash of a data block and each parent is the hash of its children, enabling efficient and verifiable comparison of large datasets.
A space-efficient probabilistic data structure that tests whether an element is possibly a member of a set, at the cost of a small chance of false positives.
A data structure that can be replicated across multiple computers, where replicas can update independently and merge their conflicts automatically without central coordination.
A program that produces its own complete source code as its only output, without reading its own file or relying on any other form of hidden input.
A malicious archive file deliberately crafted to decompress to an enormous size, intended to exhaust the disk space or memory of the system that opens it.
An algorithm that attempts connections over both IPv4 and IPv6 in parallel, preferring whichever transport responds first in order to reduce user-visible latency.
A state in which a virtual memory system spends more time swapping pages between RAM and disk than executing actual work, causing a dramatic performance collapse.
A memory allocation technique that splits blocks into two equal buddies and merges free buddies back together, trading some internal fragmentation for fast allocation and coalescing.
An optimization in which objects are duplicated only at the moment one of them is modified, allowing multiple consumers to safely share a single copy until a write occurs.
A compiler optimization that replicates the body of a loop several times to reduce loop overhead and expose instruction-level parallelism, at the cost of larger code size.
The character sequence at the start of a script file that tells the operating system which interpreter program should be used to execute the rest of the file.
The process of converting references between pointer form and another representation such as offsets or handles, typically when loading serialized objects into memory.
A process that has finished execution but still occupies an entry in the process table because its parent has not yet collected its exit status.
A class of race condition in which a system's state changes between verifying a condition and acting on it, such as checking a file's permissions and then opening it.
A memory management scheme that pre-allocates pools of objects of the same type, so frequently created and destroyed objects can be reused without repeated initialization.
A technique in which data is moved between parts of a system without the CPU copying it, typically using kernel facilities, greatly reducing latency and processor load.
A hardware or software timer that resets a system if the running program fails to reset it periodically, used to recover devices from hangs and unresponsive states.
A design pattern in which an object implementing the expected interface but doing nothing is supplied instead of a null reference, letting callers skip explicit null checks.
A fixed-size circular data structure in which the end connects back to the beginning, allowing continuous writing and reading without shifting elements in memory.
A binary numeral system in which two successive values differ by only one bit, which prevents spurious intermediate readings when values transition between states.
A retry strategy that increases the waiting time between successive failed attempts, usually doubling it, to avoid overwhelming an already struggling system.
A classic synchronization thought experiment in which philosophers sharing a limited number of forks must schedule their meals in a way that avoids deadlock and starvation.
A self-balancing search tree that keeps data sorted and allows searches, insertions, and deletions in logarithmic time by storing multiple keys in each node.
A thread that is scheduled by a runtime library or virtual machine rather than by the operating system's own native scheduler.
A special value in a data stream or variable that signals the end of data or an exceptional condition, chosen so it can never be confused with legitimate data.
